title: Module sheaves as scalar objects
statement: Let J be a Grothendieck topology on a category C and R a ring. At any common carrier universe at least the object and morphism universes of C, sheaves of R-modules are equivalent to scalar objects over R in sheaves of abelian groups. The forward functor forgets scalars on sections and remembers the scalar endomorphisms. The inverse retains the abelian sections and restriction maps and interprets the scalar endomorphisms as the module action.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: For a module sheaf, its scalar maps are natural additive endomorphisms; their ring identities follow sectionwise from the module axioms. Scalar-compatible sheaf maps are exactly linear sheaf maps.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: Evaluate a scalar object at every site object, obtaining R -> End of the abelian sections; apply ModuleCat.mkOfSMul. Naturality of scalar endomorphisms makes restriction maps linear. The underlying abelian presheaf is unchanged; the forgetful functor reflects the sheaf condition. Identity maps of sections construct the unit and counit and satisfy the triangle equation.
